producer_report.summary:
A request can now carry a priority, and `athena plan` and `athena drain` order by it. A line `Priority: high|normal|low` (any case) in the request's words sets it. Anything else, or no line, reads as normal. The order is dependencies first, then priority, then rung, then age. Without priority lines every request is normal, so the order and the parallel groups are the same as before.

A high request's prerequisites inherit its priority, so they run before unrelated older normal requests. This is what the records-history cutover (D111 job 7) needs if it has dependencies. `athena plan` prints a `priority` line for every item. `athena status` adds ` · priority high` or ` · priority low` to a request line and shows nothing for normal.

The parser is shared. `Priority::from_text` is in plan.rs and is used by both `reading::plan_entry` and `status::job_line`. Beyond the brief's list I also updated the help text in main.rs and the module doc in drain.rs. I added a CHANGELOG entry and decision D118, which records the alternatives and the cutover motivation."

open_issues: Departure from the plan: the plan listed the main.rs help text and the drain.rs module doc as edits. I made both, and they sit outside the brief's listed files.
The full cargo test was not run, so the whole suite is unchecked. Only the athena-core plan filter and the athena-cli plan filter were run (the latter also ran tests/job_plan.rs).
The decisions.md entry says the provenance is measured by the named tests; I ran them under filters, not the full suite.
The status priority suffix appears only for high and low, as in the plan (absence means normal). If the owner wants 'priority normal' on every status line, that is a one-line change in plan_suffix.
mistakes: My first display test built a plan item by hand instead of calling display::plan. I removed it and covered the plan item in tests/drain.rs instead.
learnings: Status request lines are built in display::status through plan_suffix, which appends the plan state, so the priority suffix goes there.
The latest decision in docs/decisions.md was D117, so the new entry is D118.
The Bash hook rejects tail and similar tools; use Read and Grep.
